<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1ea2363f6389a4cbd812843d670692283f52b37` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7cc88889e2294032fbb467107499c8f04d9a77da`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-file.object.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-release-read-rule.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/translations/ja-JP.objects.generated.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts, .changeset/26046-released-file-keeps-record-rule.md + packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts (the download door's authorizeDownload and its TTL choice), packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts (the reap guard's column test), packages/services/service-storage/src/index.ts (the FileRecord export), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (record file-field hydration and its closed column list), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts (additive column sync), content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx

Inputs: card #26046 (body, triage, both claims, the os-dev-report), PR #26144 (body, file list, the net diff of `0a6948210c`..`7cc88889e2` against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout; the ablation and the base-red counts are the dev's own readings and are not re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The one accept-set change, at both doors.** `judgeFileRead` gains one arm between the field-owned arm and the arm for a file no record has owned: a file whose owning record let it go, and that no record has claimed since, is judged by that record's read rule, through `readableFieldOwners`, the same function the field-owned arm asks (so a declared `fileAccessDelegate` decides here too). The download door (`buildFileReadAuthorizer`) and the record-write claim path (`buildFileReferenceReadAuthorizer`, PR #25951) both call `judgeFileRead`, so both follow it. **Right**, and a narrowing only: the uploader arm precedes it unchanged; the field-owned arm is unchanged; the arm for a file no record has owned (PR #25704's rule) is reached only when the two new columns are NULL, which is every file no record has let go and every row that predates this change; the attachments-scope arm and `public_read` (answered before the verdict at both doors) are unchanged; PR #26036's anonymous-write rule is in hunks this diff does not touch. No caller refused before is admitted now.
- **A record that no longer exists.** The arm asks the former record by id under the caller's context; a row that is gone answers nothing, so the verdict is deny for everyone but the uploader, whose arm comes first. Where the former record's object declares a delegate, the delegate's answer governs, as the ADR line already says. **Right**, and the changeset's "until it is claimed again or collected" matches.
- **Clearing the memory.** `claimFile` clears the two fields only on the path that writes the ownership columns, and that path runs only after `findReferenceableFile` has asked the write's caller through the same verdict, so the memory is cleared only by a writer who may read the former record. A refused writer's write keeps the id as written (the quiet answer of PR #25951), claims nothing, and leaves the row exactly as it was, its collection state included. A system or context-less write still claims without being asked, as PR #25951's "no caller, no question" rule already allows. **Right.** The ordering of the arm before the attachments-scope arm matches the ADR line's order and differs only for an attachments-scope file that a record's field had claimed and then let go, which is then judged by that record until claimed again or collected; consistent with the rule, named here so it is not a surprise.
- **The two `sys_file` fields.** `released_ref_object` and `released_ref_id` are nullable text fields on a platform object: additive sync adds the columns (`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`, schema-drift.ts), existing rows read NULL and take the arms they took before, and the verdict reads the row by file id (`getFile` / `findOne` with no field projection, so the new columns reach both doors). No index is needed. `copyOwnedFile` builds a copy's row field by field, so a copy never inherits them. The reap guard tests the ownership columns alone (`attachment-lifecycle.ts`), so the new fields never hold a file back from collection, as the PR says. Exposure: the fields are readable or writable only by a principal granted `sys_file` itself, exactly as `ref_object` / `ref_id` / `ref_field` are today; no permission set seeds a grant, and record hydration projects a closed column list that does not name them. That is the right exposure for platform-managed bookkeeping and should stay so; the labels and help text are abstract. **Right.**
- **Public type surface.** `FileRecord` (exported from `@objectstack/service-storage`) gains two optional members; nothing is removed or narrowed. `packages/spec/**` is untouched, as the claim required. **Right.**
- **ADR-0104, 2026-10-26 addendum, one line in the list of who the verdict admits.** Abstract, placed in the order the code asks the arms, and it matches `judgeFileRead`, `claimFile` and the collection path. It changes D3's text, so the PR is Tier H on `docs/adr/**`. **Right.**
- **Test.** `file-reference-release-read-rule.integration.test.ts` boots the shipped plugin on a real engine and asks both doors through the shipped route and the shipped hooks, for each of the four ways a file leaves its slot, under both collection settings, with the controls the rule sits beside (a file no record has owned; the uploader; a reader of the record who takes the file back). The stand-ins are the ones the family's existing door tests use. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- One changeset, `@objectstack/service-storage: patch`, `fix(storage)!:`, with the BREAKING section (Before / Now / Fix) and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The level follows the kind: `Metadata-protocol: none` (nothing a metadata author writes moves; the two fields are platform-managed), so `patch`; the narrowing keeps its banner. The disposition's facts hold on the diff: no spec key or authorable spelling moves, no export is removed or narrowed, no `objectstack migrate meta` rewrite exists. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial on the PR body and on the changeset, the same arm on both, and it is the arm the claim named as expected. The wording on the changeset, the ADR line and the PR body is abstract. **Right.**
- The four translation bundles carry the two new labels in every locale, regenerated by the gate with hand-written translated values. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions A/B (rows that predate this change).** Escalated to the maintainer with this record; this is a Tier H PR and the question is theirs. The reviewer's reading: A. Such rows hold NULL in the new fields and are judged as before; the fact the fields would hold was never recorded for them, so no exact backfill exists, and a heuristic narrowing would also refuse uploads no record has ever claimed, the quiet-failure shape. Collection, where a deployment runs it, bounds the class in time. Not blocking.
- **Signed-URL lifetime (the PR's acceptance note, confirmed in the code).** `authorizeDownload` decides the TTL from the ownership columns alone, so a URL minted for a file its record let go lives the unowned-file TTL (`presignedTtl`, default 3600 s) rather than the record-governed one (`downloadTtl`, default 300 s). Who receives a URL is this PR's rule and is right; how long an issued URL lives is a lane follow-up on the same door, and under the maintainer's standing word for this family it goes to the lane without a new card. Not blocking.
- **`#26043` remains open and its path is untouched.** Confirmed: the quiet-answer hunk is not in the diff.
- **A hand-written page states the door's arms.** `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` lists who the download door admits, by ownership; it predates PR #25704 and PR #25951 (its last change is #25240's) and now also lacks this arm. Not governed; a docs-only follow-up or a line in this PR is the owning seat's call. Not blocking.
- **PR state the reviewer did not set, for the owning seat to read.** At review time the PR is no longer draft, carries an APPROVED review on this head by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, and auto-merge is armed by that account. The PR body still says it stays draft for the maintainer; the owning seat reads the actor before touching any of it.
- **Check-runs on the head at review time.** Every concluded gate-carrying run is `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` on its latest run, an earlier run of it cancelled and superseded, `Test Core` 1/8, 2/8, 6/8 and 8/8, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the lint, type-check source and debt-ledger legs). UI legs are skipped for a diff with no `ui/` path. Those still in progress at the review's last read (`Test Core` 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 7/8, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`) have since concluded `success`: the head's runs read 36 success, 11 skipped and the one superseded cancelled run, with none failing.
